tools.name: describe_timer_link
tools.description: Given a countlink.app URL, say what it encodes: whether it is a running countdown or a not-yet-started setup link, its label, and how much time is left. Use it when someone pastes a CountLink link and asks what it is or when it ends.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_badge" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Create a countdown badge — a small image, not an <iframe> — for places embed_on_website's iframe cannot go: a GitHub README, a forum signature, a Notion page, a…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_badge · Private data: create_timer, create_agenda · Public sink: create_timer · Destructive: create_agenda.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_badge · Private data: create_timer, create_agenda · Public sink: create_timer · Destructive: create_agenda

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
